title: Agarose-based Tissue Mimicking Optical Phantoms for Diffuse Reflectance Spectroscopy
protocol: Construct the measuring systems for the diffuse reflectance and total transmittance spectra.
Use a broadband white light source, a light guide, an achromatic lens, an integrating sphere, a sample holder, an optical fiber, and a multi-channel spectrometer.
Remove the specular reflection component from the reflectance spectrum using a light trap.
Attach a hand-made cubic pedestal of polystyrene foam to the mounting plate instead of the dovetail and spring-loaded clamp assembly on the sample holder.
Connect the spectrometer and personal computer using the USB cable provided.
Attach the port adapter to a detector port of the integrating sphere.
Connect the spectrometer and the port adapter of the integrating sphere using an optical fiber.
Connect the 150 W halogen lamp light source and the light guide.
Attach the sample holder to a sample port of the integrating sphere.
Attach the light trap to an appropriate port of the integrating sphere when performing diffuse reflectance measurements.
Turn on the halogen lamp light source to illuminate a sample via the light guide and the achromatic lens.
Open the operating software of the spectrometer.
Cut out two rectangular acrylic pieces from a 2-mm-thick acrylic plate to an optional size.
Cut out an acrylic piece from a 1-mm-thick acrylic plate and cut it into a U-shaped piece for making 1-mm thick epidermal phantoms.
Remove burrs from each acrylic piece using a metal file.
Make the epidermal phantom mold by holding the 1-mm-thick U-shaped piece with two 2-mm-thick acrylic pieces and fixing them with five foldback clips.
Cut out an acrylic piece from a 5-mm-thick acrylic plate and cut it into a U-shaped piece for making 5-mm thick dermal phantoms.
Make the dermal phantom mold by holding the 5-mm-thick U-shaped piece with two 2-mm-thick acrylic pieces and fixing them with five foldback clips.
Put 500 mL of standard saline with 0.9% (w/v) NaCl in a pod.
Slowly add 5 g of agarose powder while stirring to avoid clumping.
Heat the mixture by an electric cooking heater with a 1,000 W power setting for 5 min.
Keep the mixture on low heat for 3 min once it boils.
Cool the mixture to about 70 °C.
Pour the cooled mixture into a container and keep in a constant temperature bath at 60 °C for 30 min.
Pour 100 mL of pure water into the coffee maker reservoir.
Place a filter in the coffee maker basket.
Add 24 g of ground coffee into the filter.
Turn on the coffee maker and press the brew button to begin brewing.
Put 4 mL of brewed coffee and 16 mL of saline in a glass bottle to make a coffee solution.
Put 5 mL of lipid emulsion (e.g., intralipid 10%) and 10 mL of the coffee solution into a transparent plastic cup.
Slowly add 35 mL of base material while stirring.
Aspirate the mixture into a syringe.
Inject the mixture slowly into the epidermal phantom mold to avoid bubble formation.
Cool the acrylic mold containing the mixture at 5 °C for 20 min.
Remove the foldback clips from the mold.
Slide one of the acrylic pieces outward and remove it from the mold.
Take the 1-mm-thick solidified gel phantom out of the mold.
Cut the gel phantom to the desired size using a surgical scalpel.
Place and hold the gel phantom between two slide glasses.
Prepare a dermal phantom containing oxygenated blood.
Mix 5.0 mL of lipid emulsion with 0.4 mL of whole equine blood with 45%-hematocrit in a transparent plastic cup.
Slowly add 44.6 mL of base material while stirring the mixture.
Aspirate the mixture into a syringe.
Inject the mixture slowly into the dermal phantom mold, avoiding any bubble formation.
Cool the acrylic mold containing the mixture at 5 °C for 20 min.
Remove the foldback clips from the mold.
Slide one of the acrylic pieces outward and remove it from the mold.
Take the 5-mm-thick solidified gel phantom out of the mold.
Cut the gel phantom to the desired size using a surgical scalpel.
Place and hold the gel phantom between two slide glasses.
Prepare a dermal phantom containing deoxygenated blood.
Put a dermal gel phantom containing oxygenated blood on a glass dish.
Dissolve 1 g of sodium dithionite (Na2S2O4) into 20 mL of saline in a glass bottle.
Add 0.05 g/mL of Na2S2O4 solution onto the phantom using a syringe to deoxygenate the blood in the phantom.
Place and hold the phantom between two slide glasses to prevent it drying out.
Drop 0.1 mL of saline onto a dermal phantom.
Place an epidermal phantom on the dermal phantom.
Push out any air bubbles between the layers with a fingertip.
Hold the two-layered phantom between two slide glasses to prevent it from drying out.
Position the integrating sphere for optimal diffuse reflectance measurements.
Turn off the halogen lamp light source.
Block the light path to the spectrometer using a port plug or shielding plate.
Select the Store dark command from the file menu to store a dark spectrum.
Select the Subtract dark spectrum command from the file menu to subtract the dark spectrum from the measured sample spectrum.
Turn on the halogen lamp light source.
Warm up the lamp for at least 10 minutes before acquiring a reference spectrum.
Place a standard white diffuser at the sample port of the integrating sphere.
Adjust the integration time of the spectrometer so that the peak signal intensity is approximately 75% of the spectrometer intensity maximum.
Select the Store reference command from the file menu to store a reference spectrum.
Place the epidermal phantom sandwiched by two slide glasses at the sample port.
Select the Save command from the file menu to save a diffuse reflectance spectrum to a file.
Position the integrating sphere for total transmittance measurements.
Remove the light trap from the port and attach a port plug.
Turn off the halogen lamp light source.
Block the light path using a port plug or shielding plate.
Select the Store dark command from the file menu to store a dark spectrum.
Select the Subtract dark spectrum command from the file menu to subtract the dark spectrum from the measured sample spectrum.
Turn on the halogen lamp light source by pressing the power button.
Warm up the lamp for at least 10 minutes before acquiring a reference spectrum.
Regulate the integration time of the spectrometer to show a signal that is approximately 75% of the maximum values.
Select the Store reference command from the file menu to store a reference spectrum.
Place the epidermal phantom sandwiched by two slide glasses at the sample port.
Select the Save command from the file menu to save the total transmittance spectrum to a file.
Repeat step for the dermal and two-layered phantoms.
Estimate the absorption coefficient spectrum µa(λ) and the reduced scattering coefficient spectrum µs’(λ).
Open an input file for the Monte Carlo simulation.
Fill in the values of the measured diffuse reflectance at specific wavelength range from 400 to 700 nm at 10 nm-intervals in the input data file.
Fill in the values of the total transmittance at specific wavelength range from 400 to 700 nm at 10 nm-intervals in the input data file.
Fill in the value of the phantom thickness in the input data file.
Set the refractive index n in the input data file.
Set the anisotropy factor g to 0 in the input data file.
Set the absorption coefficient µa to the appropriate value in the input data file.
Set the scattering coefficient µs to the appropriate value in the input data file.
Execute the inverse Monte Carlo simulation program.
Type the input file name and run the simulation.
Open the output file and check the final values of µa and µs.
Repeat steps for other desired wavelengths.
